hypotheses.justification: This follows from `[Finite S]`, which the theorem keeps. Mathlib has `instance (priority := 100) Module.Finite.of_finite [Finite M] : Module.Finite R M` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Basic.lean:237), and `FiniteDimensional C S` is just `Module.Finite C S`. After `omit [FiniteDimensional C S] in`, every place that needs this instance gets it by instance search: the elaboration of `exactConstantExtensionField C N S hExact` in the statement, and the helper lemmas called in the proof (`finiteDimensional_exactConstantExtension_over_base`, `isGalois_exactConstantExtension_over_frobeniusTwistField`, `finrank_exactConstantExtension_over_frobeniusTwistField`). The instance is a Prop, so by proof irrelevance the statement and the proof are unchanged. It can be deleted together with `[IsGalois C S]` as well.

This follows from `[Finite S]`. Mathlib/FieldTheory/Finite/GaloisField.lean:179 has `instance (priority := 100) {K K' : Type*} [Field K] [Field K'] [Finite K'] [Algebra K K'] : IsGalois K K'`, and that file is imported transitively through `Mathlib.FieldTheory.Finite.Extension`, which `ConstantFieldAutomorphism.lean` imports. Without the variable, instance search finds `IsGalois C S` wherever it is needed: in `exactConstantExtensionField` in the statement and in the helper lemmas used by the proof. Since `IsGalois` is a Prop, the statement is unchanged and the same proof works. It can be deleted together with `[FiniteDimensional C S]` as well.
